counterfactual_missing_items: Explicit raw statement that the thrombus caused the syncope
Raw span linking the bicuspid valve/aneurysm to the thrombus as the same diagnosis
Preoperative imaging showing the thrombus itself
decisive_items: Organized thrombus measuring 1 × 0.8 cm found at the left coronary cusp of the aortic valve, covering most of the left coronary artery's ostium
Confirmed the excised mass as an organized thrombus
Demonstrated slow blood perfusion in the left coronary artery, without evidence of significant atherosclerosis
response.rationale: R8 is the most precise acute diagnosis: the intraoperative span places an organized thrombus on the left coronary cusp of the aortic valve covering the left coronary ostium, and histopathology confirms it is an organized thrombus. R7 captures the same thrombus and slow perfusion but mislabels the location as the coronary artery lumen rather than the aortic valve cusp. R1, R6, and R4 describe structural findings but omit the thrombotic lesion that explains the syncope and exertional symptoms.

rejected.why: Only captures the ascending aortic aneurysm; ignores the bicuspid valve and the histopathologically confirmed thrombus, so it is incomplete and does not explain the acute presentation.

Combines bicuspid valve and aneurysm but omits the thrombus that explains the coronary ostial obstruction and syncope; its generator claim that intraoperative findings confirm bicuspid/aneurysm is unsupported by raw spans.
Only identifies the bicuspid valve; misses the aneurysm and the thrombotic complication, making it too narrow.
